$schema_note: Checked-in ratchet baseline for the import-hygiene CI gate (dev/quality/import_hygiene_scan.py). Read by dev/tests/test_import_hygiene_gate.py. Every entry below is a NAMED, documented exception -- never a bulk allowlist. A closing commit that fixes a violation MUST shrink the matching list in the SAME commit (relocation atomicity: the fix and the baseline shrink together).

production_family1_cross_package_private._note: HARD-ZERO (2026-07): the application.review <-> application.workflow cycle-break documented here has been structurally removed. WorkflowEvent, utc_now, InvoiceReviewRecord, and LedgerReviewRecord -- the four runtime-bound names each side needed from the other -- were extracted into a new shared leaf module, cadrumo.application._workflow_review_models, that neither application.review nor application.workflow depends on; both packages now import these names from that shared owner instead of from each other's private submodules. Every consumer outside these two packages is unaffected: they already imported through the public application.review / application.workflow facades, which keep re-exporting the same names from the new owner. The gate now asserts the production count is EXACTLY ZERO (see the corresponding hard-zero assertion in test_import_hygiene_gate.py) rather than ratcheting against a named baseline; sites stays [] and any new production Family-1 hit is a straight failure.

family2_shim_modules._note: Every module the scanner classifies as a Family-2 shim / pure-reexport surface. Now EMPTY: the last documented bridge, src/cadrumo/domain/transactions/_ids.py, is gone -- its consumers resolve TransactionId through cadrumo.core.identity, the canonical owner. The operator directive is that a symbol has exactly one home and is imported from it, so a re-export module is no longer an acceptable canonical source at all. The gate fails if ANY shim appears; do not re-add a path here to make a new bridge pass.

family2_delegate_wrapper_shims._note: The same no-standing-bridge rule as family2_shim_modules, in the syntax that evades a def-counting check: a public callable whose whole body re-calls another package's symbol with its own arguments unchanged. EMPTY by intent, and the gate fails if ANY appears. An entry here is a NAMED exception with a stated reason, keyed by (path, function) so it survives every edit that only moves the code -- it is not a mute button, and a stale entry (one whose callable is no longer a forwarding wrapper) fails the gate just as loudly as an undocumented one. Before adding an entry, prefer the fix: point the consumers at the canonical owner and delete the wrapper.

exemptions.reason: Repository surface consumed THROUGH the injected port, not by import: application/user_profile/_capsule_record.py calls objects.object_key_digest(...) on the repository it is handed, so the staticmethod is part of the port contract the application depends on. Verified by deleting it and finding that live caller; removing it would force the application to import adapters.persistence.storage.crypto directly.

Declared in both cadrumo.domain.contribuyente.assets and cadrumo.domain.contribuyente.inventory facades, zero private sources, zero cross-package consumers recorded by the scanner. Benign single-origin duplicate declaration; investigated, no action required.

family11_non_inert_package_namespaces._note: Every package __init__.py under src/cadrumo that is NOT inert, with the ways it breaches recorded SEPARATELY per namespace. The boundary rule is that a package namespace may not import, bind, lazily resolve or re-export a project symbol, and that an empty __all__ is the one binding it may carry, to document the inert boundary on purpose. The gate asserts the live set equals this set EXACTLY -- so a newly non-inert namespace fails, AND a namespace that changes which breaches it carries fails, AND an entry left behind after its namespace was made inert fails. None of the entries below is an approval: they are inherited debt, named so that new debt is distinguishable from old. The breach kinds are kept apart because they cost different amounts to close -- a re-export facade closes with a consumer sweep, a namespace holding production definitions has nowhere to point consumers AT until those definitions hard-move to a defining module first, and a lazy map hides its consumers from a static census altogether. A commit that makes a namespace inert MUST drop its entry here in the SAME commit, and a commit that changes which breaches a namespace carries MUST update its 'breaches' list in the same commit; there is no count to bump instead.

Its consumer population is effectively the whole package, so this entry closes by its own staged retirement and not as part of anyone else's sweep -- and the deferral it buys has to be re-measured rather than assumed, because a ``from core import X`` consumer pays for X's owner at import time regardless of the map.

Pure re-export facade over _protocols, _schema and its errors module. Consumer sweep only.

Breaches on all four axes at once. It carries a PEP 562 hook, defines the Typer app object, the command execution policy and its resolvers, the operator-progress emitter and a startup refusal, re-exports a further verb-input schema surface, and binds imports across adapters, application and core. The definitions include the CLI composition root, so this namespace is the one place in the tree where emptying it means deciding where an entrypoint's composition root belongs.

The one BOUNDED lazy resolution in the tree and the only entry here whose lazy map is argued rather than inherited. Its two deferred names are individually justified in the hook's own docstring and backed by a recorded import-weight measurement, which is the shape a deferral has to have to be legitimate; the namespace additionally defines the fixtures directory constant and re-exports the shared source-inventory helpers. Recorded so the gate sees it, NOT as a template: a third lazy row here is a new breach, and this entry is the reason a bare non-inert flag would have been useless.
